subject: SeedMatch discovery alignment: index scale, retrieval targets, and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Pamela Cho <pamela@seedmatch.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap & alignment — SeedMatch embeddings/rerank discovery

Hi Pamela — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. I captured what we heard on the call; please correct any details that are off.

Key pain points you shared
- Retrieval tail latency: current spikes hurt UX for sessionized product recommendations (mobile web). P99 retrievals can go above 500ms under load.
- Cost + ops: engineering has a heavy operational burden maintaining Milvus clusters and periodic rebuilds; SRE wants a simpler path to predictable unit costs.
- Upsert patterns: frequent small upserts during the day plus large nightly batch re-index (~10–12M vectors).

Current stack (as described)
- Embeddings: 1536-d vectors (in-house encoder) cached to S3 for snapshots.
- Vector DB: Milvus on k8s (self-managed), indexes are IVF-PQ for most collections.
- Serving: k8s-based API proxies, Redis for short-term session caching.
- Volume: ~1.1B total vectors across product catalogs; nightly ETL writes ~2M–3M new vectors; steady-state QPS ~800, with 2–3k bursts.

Success criteria you called out
- P95 retrieval < 60ms, P99 < 150–200ms for standard queries (50–100 tokens context for rerank).
- Cut operational overhead (fewer rebuilds, less dev time on cluster ops).
- Cost: keep incremental per-query cost low enough to support feature expansion (ballpark: <$150 per 1M queries for retrieval layer).

Initial technical observations / tradeoffs
- Indexing: for 1B+ vectors, IVF-PQ may be cheaper but can struggle with heavy upserts; HNSW hybrids or quantized HNSW on dedicated nodes could reduce latency at the cost of index size.
- Caching: prefix / session-level KV caching for hot product sets should reduce burst P99s dramatically.
- Routing: separate read-only replicas for rerank heavy paths vs. write-path nodes for upserts will stabilize tail latencies.

Proposed immediate next steps (we recommend this cadence)
1) Technical deep-dive (1hr) with your infra + data engineers — focus: upsert patterns, ETL window, and sample query distributions. (Target: next week)
2) POC data exchange: you share a sanitized sample (1–5M vectors) and sample queries; we run microbenchmarks on a Redwood-managed config and report latency/cost profiles.
3) Commercial alignment: we draft a scoped POC SOW (timeline, deliverables, success criteria) and a provisional pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted inference.

Attachments: 
- seedmatch-questions.csv (short checklist for the deep-dive)
- redwood-quick-plan.pdf (proposed POC timeline & scope)

If that all looks right, I’ll get Neha and our infra lead looped for the deep-dive scheduling. Thanks again — really liked how concretely you described the ETL cadence, that will help scope the index strategy.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Quick recap & alignment — SeedMatch embeddings/rerank discovery

Thanks Marcus — this is great and captures the call well. A few clarifications / data points from our side:

- Confirmed volumes: current production index ~1.12B vectors, 1536 dim. Nightly bulk adds ~10M vectors (these are full replacements for certain catalogs). Incremental upserts during the day are ~200–500K vectors/day.
- Query traffic: baseline QPS ~900; marketing campaigns push bursts to ~3k for short windows (2–10m).
- SLO nuance: our front-end product team measures end-to-end time; retrieval needs to be reliably <200ms P99 to keep session latency comfortable (they’ll accept <150ms ideal).
- Milvus ops pain: cluster rebuilds are manual and can take hours; we currently drain traffic and do rolling rebuilds which costs us feature time.

Regarding the sample dataset — we can provide a sanitized 5M-vector slice (no PII) and a 5000-query trace. We have an internal NDA in place with Redwood; I’ll attach the signed copy separately if needed.

Next meeting: next Wed (Nov 25) 10:00 AM PT works for our infra lead (Daniel) and me. Could you confirm availability and whether you want Neha to include a short checklist for log/trace access?

Pamela Cho
Head of Data Platforms | SeedMatch
pamela@seedmatch.ai

Marcus
